selected_applications.name: arbor_kernel
selected_applications.rationale: Passive L0 owner of contracts, types, and identifiers with zero in-umbrella dependencies. Selected as stage-zero payload because boot-manifest verification is a kernel responsibility and no Platform, Commands, or extension code may be pulled into this layer.

selected_applications.name: arbor_kernel_runtime
selected_applications.rationale: L1 runtime mechanism that hosts active Common, Signals, and Monitor services. Selected because activation-transaction mechanics belong here; the full Signals, Monitor, and os_mon surface stays a forbidden facility until a later closure.

selected_applications.name: arbor_security
selected_applications.rationale: Trusted-host identity and capability reference monitor. Selected so authorization remains a first-party in-process gate; persistence boot-cycle, authenticated sync transport, and host-provider separation remain recorded blockers.

selected_applications.name: arbor_trust
selected_applications.rationale: Trusted-host system-ceiling policy integration for URI-prefix trust rules. Selected to keep ceiling enforcement first-party; it does not make the architecture ready while host-provider separation and mutable application-env authority remain unfinished.

mandatory_host_responsibilities.rationale: Kernel owns the boot-manifest types and verification contracts that a safe boot must check before any later payload is admitted.
Runtime owns the activation transaction mechanics that must commit or roll back a safe-mode start without consulting extension applications.
Security is the identity and capability reference monitor. Safe recovery still requires this gate even while persistence and sync-transport blockers remain open.
Trust integrates system-ceiling policy so longest-prefix URI rules remain enforceable during safe recovery.
Verifying artifact bytes and honoring revocation remains a required trusted-host duty. E0B2 will bind exact payload identity; extraction from the current Platform layout is unfinished.
Containment and pre-authorization effect enforcement remain required trusted-host duties even though effect-proxy extraction is an open blocker.
Minimal boot and durable artifact-state handling remain required trusted-host duties. They are not selected application payload and their extraction is unfinished.
Mandatory pre-effect security audit remains a required trusted-host duty even though the dedicated audit spool is an open blocker.
Safe-mode management remains a required trusted-host duty. No selected application currently exposes a closed management surface.

forbidden_facilities.rationale: LLM adapters, model catalogs, and compute-node completions are cognition payload, not safe-mode recovery machinery.
OAuth clients and pooled network connections introduce remote authority and egress that safe recovery must not start.
Postgres, SQLite, and vector providers are replaceable Persistence and Historian backends, not the selected first-party safe-mode payload.
Shell execution backends can run host commands. Safe recovery must not start them as in-VM payload.
Dashboard, Voice, Gateway, and cognition stacks are operator or agent surfaces above the selected four applications.
Dynamic compile, eval, and code reload can introduce unverified code into the VM during recovery.
Skill and plugin scans plus Git fetch pull unreviewed or remote content that is not selected safe-mode payload.
Remote provider RPC before authorization can export effects or import untrusted state ahead of the reference monitor.
Unverified or third-party code must not be loaded into the safe-mode VM. E0B3 later proves executable closure.
Full Signals, Monitor, and os_mon services are observability runtime beyond the selected kernel-runtime mechanism and are not safe-mode payload.

expected_external_dependencies.rationale: A trusted host OS and installer must place the stage-zero runtime; this intent does not claim a self-hosting installer.
Protected public trust roots are host-supplied configuration that artifact and identity verification consume. They are not compiled application payload.
A local durable filesystem is the host service for artifact state and audit material. No database provider is selected.
Cryptographic entropy and a trustworthy clock are host services required for signatures, expiry, and audit timestamps.

blockers.rationale: Security still boots through a Persistence-backed authority cycle. Safe recovery cannot yet start the reference monitor without that unfinished split.
arbor_kernel_runtime has no activation-only profile that starts transaction mechanics without the full Signals, Monitor, and os_mon surface.
This intent does not bind exact built payload bytes. E0B2 must record that artifact identity before a release can claim a closed payload.
No fresh-VM measurement yet proves that only the selected payload is executable. E0B3 owns that closure.
Activation and invocation contracts are not ratified. Safe boot cannot yet name a stable ABI for entering the profile.
Security still uses cluster-scoped signals as load-bearing state sync. An authenticated sync transport is missing.
Host and replaceable-provider code are not yet separated inside Security and Trust, so the selected trusted-host role is still mixed with provider implementations.
Mutable application environment remains an authority source. Safe recovery requires fixed, verified configuration instead of live env mutation.
Public ETS tables still carry authority state. A protected registry and lifecycle transaction are required before this profile can be ready.
The mandatory synchronous pre-effect audit spool is not extracted. Audit remains a required host responsibility with no closed implementation.
Extension effect proxies are incomplete, so isolation and effect enforcement cannot yet be guaranteed from the selected applications alone.
Release packaging does not yet separate a safe-mode payload from Persistence, Historian, Shell, Dashboard, and other excluded applications.
No closed safe-mode management surface exists. Operators cannot yet manage this profile without the excluded Dashboard, Gateway, or ad hoc tools.
